Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected double-charging across Azure & GCP marketplace (May usage)

Hi Kimberly,

Quick one — our finance team picked up a discrepancy between the Azure Marketplace invoice and the GCP Marketplace invoice for May usage. It looks like ~€74k of metered usage tied to a single virtual-product (id: orbit-vp-42) was billed on both marketplaces. I attached the usage CSV and both marketplace statements for your review.

Orbit is a consolidated customer that routes some clusters through GCP (EU-west) and some through Azure (EU-north). Per our contract we consolidate and expect a single marketplace charge per billing entity. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a duplicate metering record on your side, or whether this is a cross-listing we need to split?

Time is sensitive — we need to finalize our month-end adjustments and VAT filings by June 30. Please advise the following by next Monday if possible:
- Whether Redwood will issue a credit or an intercompany offset to correct the duplicate charge
- Proposed VAT treatment for the adjustment (defer or credit) and what docs you'll provide
- Expected timeline for updated invoice(s) or credit memo

Thanks,
Helena Ramos
Head of Finance — Orbit Analytics
helena@orbit-analytics.com

Attachments: usage_report_Orbit_202905.csv, azure-usage-statement-May-2029.pdf, gcp-usage-statement-May-2029.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Helena Ramos <helena@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 12:43:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected double-charging across Azure & GCP marketplace (May usage)

Hi Helena — thank you for the clear summary and the files. We pulled the usage traces and see the same overlap you highlighted: a single producer id (orbit-vp-42) was ingested by two different marketplace ingestion pipelines during May due to a routing change we rolled out the week of May 6. That caused a duplicate metering event to be emitted to both Azure and GCP ingestors.

Immediate plan (proposed):
1) Redwood issues a credit on the lower-latency invoice (GCP) and issues a correcting invoice on the Azure listing to reflect the canonical charge — effectively an intercompany offset so Orbit only gets charged once.
2) For VAT: we can append a credit memo with an explanatory note indicating this is a billing correction for duplicate metering; Redwood will provide the credit memo and both original/adjusted invoice numbers to support Orbit's VAT filings. If Orbit prefers a VAT deferral route, we can prepare a statement of facts to enable deferral on your side — but we recommend the credit memo for audit trail.
3) Timeline: draft credit memo + corrected Azure invoice by Mon 2029-06-24 EOD Europe time; final signed documents and updated invoices by Tue 2029-06-25.

I am looping Markus (invoicing) and Marissa (marketplace ops) to validate the offsets and attach the reconciled usage. Karthik — can you review the VAT note?

Best,
Kimberly
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

- VAT handling (EU): since both invoices were issued in May, the cleanest path for Orbit's VAT reporting is a credit memo from Redwood referencing both original invoice IDs and a corrected invoice on Azure showing the single charge. This creates the audit trail for Orbit's VAT reclaim/adjustment.

I attached: recon_table.csv (line-by-line mapping), and a draft credit memo text stub.

ETA: credit memo & corrected invoice (draft) by EOD Mon Jun 24 CET; finalized docs (signed if requested) by Tue Jun 25.
